text: OVERDOSAGE In the event of hyperkalemia, discontinue the infusion immediately and institute corrective therapy to reduce serum potassium levels as necessary. The use of potassium containing foods or medications must also be eliminated. Treatment of mild to severe hyperkalemia with signs and symptoms of potassium intoxication includes the following: Dextrose Injection, USP, 10% or 25%, containing 10 units of crystalline insulin per 20 grams of dextrose administered intravenously, 300 to 500 mL per hour. Absorption and exchange of potassium using sodium or ammonium cycle cation exchange resin, orally and as retention enema. Hemodialysis and peritoneal dialysis. In cases of digitalization, too rapid a lowering of plasma potassium concentration can cause digitalis toxicity.
